Legal Standards.name: Reasonable use / beneficial use (California Constitution + Water Code)
Legal Standards.note: All water rights are limited to reasonable and beneficial use; waste/unreasonable methods are prohibited. During shortages, agencies can require conservation, change diversion practices, and scrutinize irrigation efficiency—directly affecting water deliveries and thus farm output/revenue.

Legal Standards.name: Drought emergency regulation + curtailment authority (State Water Board)
Legal Standards.note: In drought/critically dry conditions, the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) can adopt emergency regulations and curtail diversions when water isn’t available under a diverter’s priority.

Legal Standards.name: Water rights enforcement (penalties / cease-and-desist)
Legal Standards.note: Diverting without authorization can lead to enforcement, civil liability, and cease-and-desist orders. In severe shortages, the legal risk isn’t 'low productivity'—it’s illegal diversion to avoid low productivity.

Legal Standards.name: Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA)
Legal Standards.note: Groundwater Sustainability Agencies (GSAs) must manage basins to avoid 'undesirable results', often via pumping allocations, metering, fees, and projects.

Legal Standards.name: Agricultural Water Management Planning Act + measurement requirements
Legal Standards.note: Large agricultural water suppliers must prepare/update Agricultural Water Management Plans (AWMPs) and comply with measurement/efficiency planning requirements.

Legal Standards.name: Annual shortage reporting (supplier-level shortage signal)
Legal Standards.note: Certain suppliers must perform Annual Water Supply and Demand Assessments and submit Annual Shortage Reports to DWR.

Legal Standards.name: Federal environmental allocation constraints affecting deliveries (CVPIA + ESA)
Legal Standards.note: These don’t regulate 'ag productivity,' but they change project operations and water available for irrigation, especially in the Central Valley.

policies.policy_name: Reasonable use / beneficial use (California Constitution + Water Code)
policies.note: Reasonable/beneficial use and conservation norms (if achieved via efficiency, crop switching, deficit irrigation, reuse, etc.), consistent with the constitutional/section 100 policy against waste.

policies.policy_name: Agricultural Water Management Planning Act + measurement requirements
policies.note: AWMP implementation and measurement (suppliers still must plan/report regardless of revenue trend).
Revenue up can still coincide with overdraft, so SGMA obligations remain.
Supplier shortage assessment/reporting (where the entity is covered, this is the formal mechanism for declaring/recording shortage conditions and actions).

policies.policy_name: Agricultural Water Management Planning Act + measurement requirements
policies.note: AWMP operational measures (allocation rules, delivery scheduling, conservation programs) as part of planned shortage response.

policies.policy_name: Reasonable use / beneficial use (California Constitution + Water Code)
policies.note: Reasonable use review pressure increases during shortages, especially if visible inefficiencies persist.
Still not inherent. Risk emerges if parties respond by diverting outside legal right or failing required reporting if applicable.

policies.policy_name: Drought emergency regulation + curtailment authority (State Water Board)
policies.note: SWRCB drought emergency actions / curtailments when conditions support them (curtailments are explicitly authorized to match diversions to priority/availability). Local or watershed-specific emergency regulations may apply.
SGMA pumping allocations / ramp-down implementation in stressed basins to avoid undesirable results.

policies.policy_name: Federal environmental allocation constraints affecting deliveries (CVPIA + ESA)
policies.note: Federal project operational constraints (CVPIA/ESA) can be a significant cause of reduced allocations in some areas/years.
If curtailed users continue diverting, that can become unauthorized diversion exposure (civil liability structure in section 1052; SWRCB enforcement).

policies.policy_name: Drought emergency regulation + curtailment authority (State Water Board)
policies.note: Curtailments and/or emergency regulations are much more likely in severe scarcity because the statute expressly contemplates emergency rules and curtailment when water is unavailable under priority.
Aggressive SGMA compliance actions (hard caps/allocations, fees, enforcement) to stop significant and unreasonable basin impacts.
Supplier shortage reporting and drought-stage restrictions (where covered), and intensified shortage allocation/rotation at irrigation-district/supplier level.

policies.policy_name: Federal environmental allocation constraints affecting deliveries (CVPIA + ESA)
policies.note: Federal CVP/ESA constraints often become binding in dry years, reducing delivered water.

policies.relationship: Where violation is most likely to occur
policies.note: Diverting/pumping contrary to curtailment/emergency conditions or without right -> enforcement tools (CDOs) and civil liability under section 1052 become central.

policies.policy_name: Reasonable use / beneficial use (California Constitution + Water Code)
policies.note: Reasonable use / anti-waste scrutiny tends to intensify when scarcity is extreme (e.g., pressure to stop clearly inefficient methods).

Governing Agencies.name: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB)
Governing Agencies.note: Emergency regulations, curtailments, water-right enforcement, cease-and-desist orders.

Governing Agencies.name: California Department of Water Resources (DWR)
Governing Agencies.note: AWMP guidance/review support, shortage assessment program administration, statewide planning/technical standards.

Governing Agencies.name: Groundwater Sustainability Agencies (GSAs)
Governing Agencies.note: SGMA compliance via pumping allocations, projects, and enforcement to avoid undesirable results.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates federal projects (e.g., CVP) whose allocations materially affect ag supply.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (USFWS) / NOAA Fisheries
Governing Agencies.note: ESA consultation drivers affecting operations/diversions and project pumping constraints.
